The medical LLM keeps deflecting general questions. I need to make sure we only run the generic container by default and swap to medical only when the user explicitly selects it.
Battery brownout is still an issue. The Jetson draws too much current during model loading and the power bank can't keep up. I might need a regulated 5V 4A supply instead.
Whisper is hallucinating on background noise again. Getting phantom transcripts like thank you and bye when nobody is talking. Need to add a blocklist filter.

I want Aura to be more proactive. Like if it knows I have a pitch meeting coming up, it should think about what I need to prepare and bring it up when I next talk to it. That's what Aura Perpetual is about.
The voice cloning with Chatterbox sounds good but it's inconsistent. Sometimes it nails my voice, other times it sounds robotic. Kokoro is more consistent but doesn't clone. Tradeoff.

Rafael asked me about the complication system. Each complication is like a watch complication — a mini app that sits on the dial. Settings, weather, health metrics, concierge. Up to 4 at a time plus the center Topics display.
I need to set up SSH access before shipping the Puck so I can remotely debug when testers hit issues. Password auth should be fine for now, we can do key-based later.
The boot animation looks great. The Falcon sweep with the Aura intro music, then voice enrollment, then the tour of complications. Really polished first impression.

I'm worried about the response latency. Right now it's about 4 to 5 seconds from end of speech to first TTS output. I want to get that under 3 seconds. The thinking fillers help mask it but it's still too slow.

Looking at the competitive landscape. Humane flopped, Rabbit is struggling. But I think on-device is the right bet. People don't want another cloud subscription. They want something that works without internet.
The RAG system is working well for document ingestion. I uploaded the Ledger AI pitch deck and now Aura can answer questions about our company from the actual document. Very useful for demo.
I should create a proper onboarding flow for new users. Voice enrollment, name capture, tour of features, maybe ask about their interests so Aura can personalize from day one.

Thinking about the multi-user angle. The Puck sits in a room — multiple family members should be able to use it. Voice profiles for identification, separate conversation histories, personalized responses per person.
We need to figure out the manufacturing side. The current Pucks are hand-assembled. If we want to do a small batch of 50 to 100 units, we need a contract manufacturer. Maybe Shenzhen.
The Perpetual engine is going to be the killer feature. Nobody else has an AI that thinks about you when you're not talking to it. It's like having a chief of staff who's always preparing your brief.
Aura, what are the FDA requirements for a Class II medical device? I need to understand if our medical mode needs 510k clearance or if we can classify as wellness.

I just got off a call with Dr. Mehta from Stanford. She said the biggest problem in her clinic is patients not understanding their discharge instructions. She literally said patients forget 80 percent of what the doctor tells them by the time they get home. Aura could solve that.

The pitch deck needs work. Slide 7 about our competitive moat is weak. Everyone says privacy but nobody believes it until they see the device working offline. The demo IS the moat. I need to lead with the live demo in every pitch.

Rafael just texted me, he said the puck crashed three times today. All during the boot sequence. I think it is the power supply. The USB-C power delivery negotiation might be failing under load when the GPU spins up for Whisper.

What is the typical power draw of a Jetson Orin Nano under full GPU load? I measured 12 watts but the power bank is rated for 15 watts so theoretically it should work. Unless there are transient spikes.

I keep going back and forth on B2B versus B2C. The healthcare VCs want B2B because the sales cycle is predictable and the margins are better. But I got into this to help regular people, not to sell to hospital procurement departments. Maybe I can do both — medical B2B for revenue and consumer B2C for impact.

Aura, remind me about the Humane AI Pin failure. What went wrong with their launch? I remember reading the reviews were terrible but I want to understand specifically what they got wrong so we do not repeat it.

Just ran the numbers. At our current burn rate with no revenue we have runway until August. If the seed round closes by June we are fine. If it slips to September we are in trouble. I need a plan B. Maybe contract development work on the side to extend runway.

Rafael says the voice response is too slow. He timed it at 6 seconds from when he stops talking to when Aura starts responding. He says it feels like talking to someone with a bad internet connection. The thinking fillers help but he can tell they are filler. We need to get this under 3 seconds or it breaks the conversational illusion.

I wonder if we should use speculative decoding. Pre-generate likely responses while the user is still talking based on partial transcript. Risky because if we guess wrong we waste GPU cycles. But if we guess right we cut latency by 40 percent.

The voice cloning demo blew the investors away. When Aura responded in a voice that sounded like them, you could see the moment they got it. That is our secret weapon for fundraising. Every demo should include voice cloning.

Talked to a contract manufacturer in Shenzhen today. Minimum order is 500 units at 180 dollars per unit. That is 90 thousand dollars just for manufacturing. Plus the Jetson modules are 249 each. So fully loaded cost per unit is about 450 dollars. If we sell at 699 that is 55 percent margin. Not great but workable for hardware.

I am exhausted. Been debugging the Whisper hallucination issue for 8 hours straight. Background noise in my apartment keeps triggering phantom transcripts. Thank you, goodbye, you. It is like Aura is hearing ghosts. The spectral filter helps but it is not enough. I need a blocklist approach on top of the signal processing.

Sometimes I wonder if I am crazy for doing this. Everyone in AI is going cloud. OpenAI, Google, Anthropic. And here I am trying to run a 7 billion parameter model on a 250 dollar dev board. But every time I see it work, every time someone talks to Aura and it just works without any internet, I know this is the right path.

My mom called today. She asked what I am working on. I tried to explain Aura and she said why would I need that when I have Siri. That is exactly the problem. People do not understand the privacy angle until you explain that Siri sends everything to Apple. When I told her that she was horrified. That is our marketing angle right there.

Note to self. The medical LLM needs to handle medication interactions. Dr. Mehta specifically asked if Aura could cross reference a patient medications and flag dangerous combinations. That is a killer feature for elderly patients on multiple prescriptions. Could literally save lives.

Had the pitch meeting with Khosla today. They liked the demo but pushed back on the market size. They said on device AI is niche and the real money is in cloud. I disagree but I did not argue. I just asked them to try using Aura for a week without internet and see if they change their mind. They took a puck.

Three VCs have now asked about our data strategy. They want to know how we monetize user data. When I say we do not collect user data they look confused. One of them literally said that is a feature not a business model. I need a better answer for the privacy-as-value-prop question.

Aura, what are the top telehealth platforms in the US by market share? I want to explore partnerships. If we can integrate Aura as a post-visit companion for telehealth patients that could be our B2B entry point. Patient calls doctor on Teladoc, then Aura helps them understand and follow the instructions afterward.

The AuraConnect app is working on Mac now. Bluetooth pairing takes about 3 seconds. Next step is syncing conversation history so you can review on your laptop what you talked about with Aura. Rafael wants a search feature so he can find specific conversations.

I realized the complication system is actually our platform play. If third party developers can build complications, Aura becomes a platform not just a product. Think watchOS for voice AI. Weather complications, health tracking, smart home control, all running locally. That is how we build the ecosystem.

Huge breakthrough today. Got the response latency down to 3.2 seconds by overlapping Whisper transcription with LLM prefill. The trick is to start the LLM inference with the partial transcript while Whisper is still processing the last few frames. Saves about 800 milliseconds.

The 7B model on CPU is way too slow for conversation. Five minutes per response. But for background thinking it is perfect. Nobody cares if the overnight analysis takes 30 minutes. Quality over speed for that use case.

I need to hire someone. I cannot do hardware, software, ML, business development, fundraising, and customer support all by myself. The first hire should probably be a firmware engineer who can own the hardware reliability. The brownout crashes and power management issues are eating all my time.
Aura, what is the average salary for a firmware engineer in the Bay Area? Also what about remote firmware engineers. I cannot afford Bay Area rates on our seed budget.

Dr. Mehta introduced me to the head of digital health at Kaiser. They are interested in a pilot program. 20 units in a geriatric ward for post-discharge patient education. If this works it could be our first real customer. Revenue by Q3 is possible.

I have been thinking about what happens if the seed round does not close. Worst case scenario planning. I could pivot to a consulting model, use the Aura tech stack to build custom on-device AI solutions for enterprises. It is not what I want to do but it would generate revenue and prove the technology.

Rafael had a great idea. He said what if Aura could detect when someone is confused based on their tone of voice and automatically simplify its explanation. Like if a patient sounds uncertain Aura rephrases in simpler language. That would be incredible for the medical use case.

The Kaiser pilot could be huge but I am nervous about it. If something goes wrong with the medical mode and it gives bad advice to a real patient that is a liability nightmare. I need to talk to a healthcare attorney about our risk exposure. Maybe we need to frame it as an educational tool not a medical device.

Every night this week I have been up until 2 AM coding. I know it is not sustainable but there is so much to build and so little time. The seed round timeline is driving everything. I need the demo to be flawless by the end of this month.
Aura, explain the difference between 510k clearance and de novo classification for medical devices. Also what is a predicate device and do we need one.

I sent 3 pucks out this week. Rafael, Dr. Mehta, and the Khosla partner. That is 3 units in the wild generating real usage data. If the boot sequence holds up and nobody hits the brownout crash, we are golden. Fingers crossed.

The privacy angle is resonating more than I expected. A journalist from Wired reached out after seeing our GitHub. She wants to do a story on on-device AI as the counter-narrative to big tech surveillance. This could be huge for visibility. I need to prepare talking points.

I just had a scary thought. What if Apple announces on-device Siri at WWDC this year. That would destroy our differentiation overnight. I need to think about what makes Aura defensible beyond just being local. The medical mode, the open platform, the hackability. Those are things Apple will never do.

I showed the Perpetual briefing feature to my advisor. He said it reminds him of the CIA presidential daily brief. That is exactly what I was going for.

My runway is until August. If I do not close the seed round by June I am in trouble.
The ElevenLabs API costs are killing me. 45 dollars last month just for TTS. Kokoro on device is the right call.

Humble.Pi: Aura - when you are used in a clinical environment, What are the risks? For example halucinations and "made up" answers
Aura: Good question. Using AI like me in a clinical setting comes with some serious risks. Hallucinations—where I might make up information or provide incorrect advice—are a big one. There's also the risk of misinterpreting patient data, which could lead to wrong diagnoses or treatment recommendations. Privacy and security are major concerns too, especially when handling sensitive health information. It’s crucial that any AI used in healthcare is thoroughly tested and monitored to minimize these risks.

Humble.Pi: Aura, can you answer this question above on liability?
Aura: Sure. In a clinical setting, if an AI system like me were to give incorrect advice that harmed a patient, the legal responsibility could fall on several parties:

1. **The Developers**: If the AI was designed and built by a specific company or individual, they could be held liable for any flaws in the system.
2. **The Healthcare Provider**: The doctors or clinics using the AI could also be held responsible if they relied on the AI's advice without proper oversight.
3. **The Institution**: Hospitals or healthcare institutions that implement the AI could face liability if they didn't follow best practices or regulations.

It’s a complex area, and legal frameworks are still evolving to address these issues. But generally, the key is ensuring that AI systems are used responsibly and with appropriate safeguards in place.
